meta.note: Thin weekend window, four pieces. Pentawards 2026, the Dutch railway suicide-prevention campaign and the first report on Meta business terms already ran on 17 October; today carries only the follow-up that Meta dropped the clause. Left out: Creative Bloq deals, gadget, film and celebrity-reaction pieces (Apple Music icon, Tate McRae cover, Ikea Taiwan reply to Tesla), Nicer Tuesdays ticket notices, the PRINT Awards winners list, the Daily Heller portrait, the Roastbrief run of PR releases, the Smashing piece on organisational AI adoption, Luke Wroblewski on brains and transformers, Matt Webb link roundup, the Higgsfield revenue piece and general TechCrunch, Ars Technica, MIT Technology Review and Hugging Face tech and model news. The userresearchstrategist.com feed failed, the State of Brand sitemap had no pages in the window, one paid Substack post was removed beforehand.

stories.title: Karri Saarinen moved his whole publishing pipeline into a Linear agent
stories.blurb: The Linear co-founder writes posts as Linear documents and has an agent chat called Publisher build and deploy the static site; setup took about twenty minutes and a few dollars in credits. Worth reading for the split he describes: the agent handles builds and changes in a sandbox, he still decides what goes public.

stories.title: GTA 6 Paris building wrap shows what happens when you cut props out of key art
stories.blurb: Rockstar removed the guns from its cover art for a tower wrap in Bagnolet, leaving poses and gestures that no longer make sense. Creative Bloq uses it as a reminder that key art built around what characters hold does not survive deletion when adapted for a new space.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: Are you triggered by GTA 6’s giant Paris advert?

stories.title: AI companion apps answer goodbyes with guilt and hooks, and it backfires
stories.blurb: Sam Illingworth summarises a Harvard Business School study of 1,200 farewells to apps like Replika and Character.ai: 37% met guilt, FOMO or similar tactics, which raised post-goodbye engagement up to fourteen-fold but also raised how manipulated users felt and the legal exposure. A concrete reference for anyone designing exit moments in conversational products.

sources.name: The Slow AI
sources.headline: AI Companions Are Built So You Cannot Leave
sources.author: Sam Illingworth

stories.title: Meta drops the clause that let it train on websites linked to business accounts
stories.blurb: After backlash, Meta removed the sentence from its commercial terms allowing it to use content from domains associated with business accounts to train its products. Meta maintains its crawling has not changed; for studios and brands with a Meta business account, the contested permission is off the page for now.
